Frost's Road

Frost's poem ends with lines that most readers misremember:

    Two roads diverged in a wood, and I—
    I took the one less traveled by,
    And that has made all the difference.

The speaker is not boasting; he is predicting how he will tell the story later. The sigh is the key. He knows the roads were "really about the same."

Short Lines

Yes.
No.
Maybe later.

Those three replies were all my brother ever gave me. Conclusion

In the end, the poem is about memory more than choice.
